Subject: Request for Written Consent to Sublet — [ADDRESS_1]

Dear Landlord/Property Manager,

I, Alex Kim, the original tenant under the lease for [ADDRESS_1], request your express written consent to sublet the dwelling to Jordan Rivera from June 1, 2027 through July 28, 2027. The lease requires express written consent for a sublet and provides for a $150 administrative fee; it also states that the original resident(s) remain liable for lease obligations through the original term, including damage caused by a subtenant (lease p. 3).

Please confirm in writing whether you approve this sublet, whether the $150 fee is due and how it should be paid, and any required subtenant screening, insurance, or other approval steps. Please also confirm how the lease’s automatic month-to-month renewal and 60-day written-notice provision apply after July 31, 2027 (lease p. 1), and whether your consent is limited to the dates above.

The subtenant will be given the applicable lease rules. I understand that this request does not release me or any other original resident from obligations under the master lease. Please provide your written decision before the proposed move-in.

Sincerely,
Alex Kim
[Contact information]
docs.agreement_md_en:
# Sublease Agreement (Draft — Subject to Landlord’s Written Consent)

**Premises:** [ADDRESS_1]  
**Sublessor:** Alex Kim  
**Subtenant:** Jordan Rivera  
**Sublease term:** June 1, 2027 through July 28, 2027. Occupancy begins and ends on these dates, subject to the landlord’s written approval. The sublease does not extend the master lease or grant occupancy beyond the approved term.

## 1. Required consent and controlling lease
This agreement is conditional on the landlord’s express written consent, as required by the master lease (lease p. 3). Attach the written consent to this agreement. The master lease and its applicable rules are incorporated here. If this agreement conflicts with the master lease or the landlord’s written approval, the master lease/approval controls. The sublessor remains responsible to the landlord for obligations under the master lease, including subtenant-caused damage, through the original lease term (lease p. 3). This sublease does not bind the landlord to extend or renew the master lease.

## 2. Rent and payment
Monthly rent is **$2,150**, matching the master lease amount (lease p. 1). Rent is payable in advance on or before the 1st of each month. The parties must write and initial the agreed amount and due date for the partial July 1–28, 2027 period before signing: **$________**, due **________**. Do not assume a proration formula unless both parties agree in writing. Payment method/recipient: **________**. The master lease states that rent is due by the 1st and provides for a $50 initial late charge if rent is not paid by the 10th; the parties should confirm in writing how any such lease charge applies to this sublease (lease p. 1).

## 3. Security deposit and escrow
The subtenant will pay a security deposit of **$1,500** to Rentrail escrow, to be held until the return inspection and handled under applicable Connecticut deposit requirements. Before accepting the funds, the sublessor must ensure the deposit is placed in a Connecticut financial-institution escrow account for the subtenant’s benefit and provide written notice stating the amount held and the institution’s name and address within the statutory period (CT-47a-21-h1; CT-47a-21-h4). Confirm the escrow institution and account details in the receipt/notice; “Rentrail escrow” alone does not supply those details.

The deposit may be applied only to lawful, actual amounts owed or damages supported by an itemized written notice; ordinary wear is not a damage deduction. Any undisputed balance and accrued interest must be returned with the required itemization by the applicable legal deadline. The stated target return date is **August 18, 2027**, subject to any later deadline required by the statutory forwarding-address rule (CT-47a-21-d2; CT-47a-21-a14; DOB-itemize). The sublessor will account for and pay applicable deposit interest (CT-47a-21-i). No deduction may be made without an itemized explanation and amount.

## 4. Utilities
- **Electricity:** Subtenant is responsible for electricity during the sublease term, paid directly to the electric utility where feasible, consistent with the master lease (lease p. 4).
- **Water, sewer, and trash:** Sublessor will pay these charges and will not pass them through to the subtenant under this agreement. The master lease bills these through Conservice, with allocation based on occupants and square footage and a $3.95 monthly service/administrative fee (lease p. 4).
- **Heat and hot water:** The master lease says these are provided by the landlord (lease p. 4).
- **Internet and cable:** The master lease places responsibility on the tenant; the parties must specify whether these are included or separately arranged: **________** (lease p. 4).

## 5. Master-lease rules and care
The subtenant agrees to follow all applicable master-lease requirements and building rules provided with this agreement, including:
- Keep the premises clean and safe; use plumbing, appliances, and building systems reasonably; do not damage or remove property (lease p. 2; CT-47a-11).
- Submit repair requests through the online resident portal or by signed written request delivered to the office. Use the landlord’s 24-hour emergency maintenance service for emergencies (lease p. 2).
- Maintain personal liability insurance with at least **$100,000 per occurrence** for residents and guests and provide proof before move-in, as required by the master lease (lease p. 2). The parties must confirm with the landlord that the subtenant’s policy satisfies its requirements.
- Follow applicable access, safety, occupancy, and other written house rules supplied by the landlord. Attach any additional rules: **________**.

## 6. Move-in handoff and condition record
The parties will complete a joint handoff inspection on or before June 1, 2027, record existing defects and conditions in writing, and take dated photographs. Provide the subtenant a copy. The master lease requires defects, damage, and safety or pest concerns to be recorded and returned within 48 hours after move-in (lease p. 2). The parties should submit the applicable form within that period. The sublessor will provide the keys/access devices and document the number delivered.

## 7. Repairs and damage
The subtenant will promptly report needed repairs using the master-lease method and notify the sublessor of emergencies. The subtenant is responsible only for actual, reasonable, legally recoverable costs attributable to the subtenant or the subtenant’s guests, not pre-existing conditions or ordinary wear. The sublessor remains responsible to the landlord under the master lease as stated above (lease p. 3). Any proposed deposit deduction must be itemized and supported with the nature and amount of the claim (CT-47a-21-d2; DOB-itemize).

## 8. Return inspection and move-out
The parties will schedule a joint return inspection for July 28, 2027, or another mutually agreed time close to move-out. The subtenant will remove personal belongings, leave the premises clean, and return all keys and access devices. The master lease requires a move-out inspection and return of keys/access devices (lease p. 3); it states that each unreturned key may trigger a $75 rekeying charge (lease p. 1). Record the condition with dated photographs and compare it with the signed handoff record. The subtenant may attend the inspection.

The subtenant will give the sublessor a forwarding address in writing before departure. The sublessor will provide the deposit balance, accrued interest, and any written itemized damages notice by the applicable Connecticut deadline (CT-47a-21-d2; CT-47a-21-i).

## 9. Master lease end and notices
The master lease’s stated initial term ends July 31, 2027 and automatically renews month-to-month unless either side gives at least 60 days’ written notice (lease p. 1). This sublease ends July 28, 2027 and does not by itself satisfy or alter any notice obligation under the master lease. The sublessor must confirm the master-lease status and any required notice with the landlord. The subtenant has no right to remain after the approved sublease end date without a new written agreement and any required landlord consent.

## 10. Signatures
This draft is not effective until landlord consent is obtained and the parties complete all blanks, including the July partial-period rent and internet/cable arrangement.

ruling.ruling_en: Approve the computed $88.10 electricity share. The comparison supports that the wall crack is new, but no invoice or quote establishes its actual reasonable repair cost; approve no damage deduction now and hold $200 in escrow pending documentation. Release $1,211.90 of the $1,500 principal now, plus any applicable accrued interest on the amount being returned; adjust the held amount to the documented reasonable cost, not exceeding $200. Provide an itemized written notice and return the balance and interest by the applicable statutory deadline. [CT-47a-21-a7] [CT-47a-21-a14] [CT-47a-21-d2] [CT-47a-21-j2] [DOB-itemize]
ruling.ruling_ko: 계산된 전기요금 분담금 88.10달러를 승인합니다. 비교 자료는 벽 균열이 새 손상임을 뒷받침하지만, 실제 합리적인 수리비를 확인할 영수증이나 견적이 없으므로 현재 손상 공제는 승인하지 않고 증빙이 제출될 때까지 200달러를 에스크로에 보류합니다. 원금 1,500달러 중 1,211.90달러와 반환 대상 금액에 적용되는 발생 이자를 지금 반환하세요. 보류액은 증빙된 합리적 수리비에 맞춰 조정하되 200달러를 넘을 수 없습니다. 항목별 서면 통지와 잔액 및 이자를 법정 기한 내 반환해야 합니다. [CT-47a-21-a7] [CT-47a-21-a14] [CT-47a-21-d2] [CT-47a-21-j2] [DOB-itemize]
ruling.letter_en:
Subject: Sublet escrow settlement — [PERSON_1] and [PERSON_2]

Dear [PERSON_1] and [PERSON_2],

This is the proposed settlement of the $1,500 sublet escrow for the tenancy ending July 28, 2027. The computed June 1–30, 2027 electricity share is $88.10 (bill 3, Shoreline Electric), which is approved. The comparison states that hand-off record #36 showed no wall findings and return evidence #42 shows a bedroom-wall crack. The record provided does not give the dates for those exhibits; please confirm their dates. Exhibit E42 supports the existence of new damage, but no repair invoice or quote has been provided. Accordingly, no wall-repair deduction is approved now; $200 will remain in escrow temporarily pending documentation of the actual reasonable repair cost. The nearby “Cracked!!” writing is not a separate charge.

Please release $1,211.90 of the $1,500 principal now, plus applicable accrued interest on the amount being returned. After receiving a repair invoice or quote, provide it to both parties and release any part of the $200 hold that is not supported by the actual reasonable cost. Any final deposit accounting should itemize the nature and amount of the utility and any supported damage claim, and return the balance and applicable interest by the deadline under Conn. Gen. Stat. §47a-21(d)(2). A tenant who sublets is treated as a landlord for this purpose under §47a-21(a)(7); allowable tenant obligations include utility payments under §47a-21(a)(14), and a good-faith claim requires written notice under §47a-21(j)(2). The notice should also follow the Connecticut Department of Banking itemization guidance [DOB-itemize].

Please reply within 10 days confirming the payment, the repair documentation plan, and the applicable forwarding address and return deadline. This proposal does not treat the provisional $200 estimate as a proven repair cost.

Sincerely,
[PERSON_2]
ruling.letter_ko_summary: [PERSON_1]과 [PERSON_2]에게 보내는 합의 통지입니다. 계산된 6월 전기요금 88.10달러는 승인하고, 벽 균열 수리비는 증빙이 없으므로 공제 승인 없이 최대 200달러를 잠정 에스크로 보류합니다. 원금 1,211.90달러와 반환 대상 이자를 지금 반환하고, 증빙된 합리적 수리비를 넘는 보류액은 반환하도록 요청합니다. 기록에 전시물 E36 및 E42의 날짜가 없어 날짜 확인도 요청합니다. 10일 내 회신과 적용되는 법정 기한에 따른 항목별 정산을 요구합니다.
